sn47.13:1.1: This event follows [sn47.12]() at Nāḷandā and precedes [sn47.14]() at Ukkacelā on the Vajjian shore of the Ganges, so the Buddha must have been somewhere on the road between them, not in Sāvatthī. Sāvatthī was the default location for teachings and it is often ascribed as a matter of convention.
sn47.13:1.3: The commentaries identify “novice Cunda”, who reported the deaths of Sāriputta ([sn47.13:1.3]()) and Mahāvīra ([dn29:2.1](), [mn104:3.1]()), as Sāriputta’s younger brother, explaining that the title “novice” was a nickname that persisted from the time he ordained as a young novice.
sn47.13:6.3: At SN 35.84 I render palokadhamma as “wear out” to pun (feebly) with world. Here the sense must be fall, drop.
